title: Organic, non-GMO, grass-fed... what do they all mean?
summary: Two farm podcasters argue many food labels are marketing, covering grass-fed, organic, rBST-free, non-GMO and natural claims.

assertions.quote: grass-fed doesn't necessarily tell you about Animal Welfare you can be still in a confined animal feeding operation
upwards of 75% of our grass-fed cattle here in the United States or grass-fed beef in the grocery store is imported

verdicts.note: Industry analyses have estimated that most US grass-fed beef at retail comes from Australia, New Zealand and South America.

assertions.quote: for me I feel like organic is more of a farming practice than like a health claim

verdicts.note: The USDA defines organic as a production standard and makes no claim that organic food is safer or more nutritious.
The organic standard is written as a list of allowed and prohibited substances and methods for production and handling (7 CFR 205.105) and makes no nutrition or health requirement.
The organic label certifies approved production and handling methods; ERS notes the USDA organic regulations do not address the health and safety of organic foods.

assertions.quote: they have not gone through the USDA organic certification or whatever but their practices to me are even better
there is officially no milk on the Shelf from cows treated with RBST

verdicts.note: Use of rBST has fallen to a small minority of herds and most processors refuse it, but it is still approved and not entirely gone.

assertions.quote: it used to be that everything was labeled natural and then we all became very suspect of that
one of the funniest labels I've ever seen in the grocery store was a non-GMO salt

verdicts.note: Only a handful of crops have commercial GE varieties, yet non-GMO claims appear on many products that could never be genetically engineered.

assertions.quote: with like macronutrients and the nutrients they really do look identical

verdicts.note: Compositional studies reviewed by the National Academies found approved GE crops nutritionally equivalent to conventional ones, apart from deliberately altered traits.

assertions.quote: now they are absolutely for like a marketing purpose
